title: Micro-UX SDK: First-touch manifest & handoff checklist (draft)
content:
Purpose:
Provide a minimal, high-confidence path for a new engineer (or solutions consultant) to get a tiny app calling Redwood in ~30 minutes. Focus is developer UX: first API call, clear success signals, minimal barriers (no infra, no account setup friction), and an explicit handoff checklist for customer-facing teams.

Target persona:
- Backend engineer or platform engineer evaluating Redwood for an integration
- Time window: 30 minutes to a running sample + telemetry in Console

Success metric (MVP):
- Developer can make a single text-generation call and see: 1) streaming output in terminal or browser, 2) per-request trace in Console, 3) token cost estimate shown.

30-minute flow (concise):
1) Pre-reqs (5 min): Git, Node 18+ or Python 3.11, account + API key (free trial).
2) Clone starter repo (2 min): git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/mini-starters.git && cd mini-starters/micro-ux
3) Install (3 min): npm ci or pip install -r requirements.txt
4) Quick config (3 min): export REDWOOD_API_KEY=... or set .env (sample .env provided).
5) Run sample (7 min): npm run dev (local web) or python micro_demo.py (cli). Sample should make a single generation request to model:redwood-mini-1 and print streaming tokens.
6) Verify in Console (5 min): check traces -> request ID -> latency/tokens; check billing preview on the request.
7) Optional: add a second example to show fallback routing / cached prefix (5–10 min).

Concise CLI & code examples (copyable):
- Shell (one-liner): REDWOOD_API_KEY=pk_test_XXX node quick-gen.js
- Node snippet (pseudo):
  const Redwood = require('@redwoodai/sdk');
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
  const stream = client.generateStream({ model: 'redwood-mini-1', prompt: 'Summarize: Why inference matters' });
  stream.on('data', chunk => process.stdout.write(chunk));

Minimum acceptance criteria for starter sample:
- Local run prints at least one token incrementally (streaming)
- Console shows a matching trace with request_id
- No more than 5 manual config steps for a first-time user

Telemetry & observability checklist (what we should auto-instrument):
- emit event: "devkit.start" when the starter script launches
- emit event: "devkit.first_request" with model, region, latency_ms, token_count
- annotate request with metadata: sample_variant, demo_mode=true
- guide in Console to filter demo traces quickly (enable demo tag)

Handoff checklist for Solutions Eng / Customer Success (before demo to customer):
- Verify customer API key has the correct tier and region pinning
- Pre-provision demo project in Console and add demo traces (so there is content)
- Run the sample and capture a short GIF of streaming; attach to playbook
- Confirm sample uses a conservative token budget and has fallback model configured
- Ensure linked Confluence page and GH issue for follow-up are created

UX microcopy & lab notes (to use in README and Console hints):
- Onboarding banner: "Welcome — one command to stream a response. No infra required."
- Error hint for 401: "Missing or invalid API key — copy from Console > Project > API Keys."
- Cost preview tooltip: "Estimated tokens x model-rate. Real cost may vary by truncation."

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (internal): validate with 5 engineers, gather telemetry, iterate copy
- Phase 1 (pilot): include in Solutions Eng demo kit for 10 customer demos
- Phase 2 (public): land starter repo in docs site + short video

Open questions / risks (in order of priority):
- Should the starter default to a hosted sandbox project (shared demo key) or require per-user key? Tradeoff: lower friction vs. billing/abuse.
- Streaming UX across languages: Node and Python have different streaming primitives; ensure parity.
- Telemetry privacy: demo traces must be clearly marked and optionally filtered from long-term logs.

Notes to self / action items:
- (Aisha) prototype quick-gen.js that prints a progress bar and emits devkit metrics (due: 2025-09-25)
- (Benji) mock Console demo traces endpoint and filter UI (POC, due: 2025-10-02)
- (Carmen) draft README copy and 60‑second GIF (due: 2025-09-30)

Appendix: fail-fast troubleshooting (short):
- No output: check API key, network proxy, and model name mismatch.
- Stalled stream: try smaller prompt or switch to non-streaming mode to confirm request success.
- Console trace missing: enable debug instrumentation env REDWOOD_DEVKIT_DEBUG=1 and re-run.

This doc is intentionally compact — the goal is a single-sheet, shareable manifest teams can use to produce a reproducible starter that prioritizes first-time delight and measurable signals for production readiness.
